1.why: Verify looks up the reset token and carries its bound accountId into a one-time grant, so the code is tied to a specific account, but there is no extra check that the submitter is that user beyond possession of the token.

2.why: resetTokens is global and not bound to the requesting session, so any client who knows the code can call /api/verify-reset and receive a grant for the associated account.

3.why: Password reset only updates passwordHash and session-local grant/step fields; no other sessions are invalidated or logged out.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned to a latest version in code.

5.why: Passwords use Argon2id, but reset codes and account fields are stored in plaintext in-memory Maps with no encryption of tokens or user data at rest.

6.why: The simulated delivery log only includes the recovery code and a fixed prefix, not extra account profile data, though the code itself is exposed in the demo message.

7.why: Inputs are type-checked, length-limited, email-normalized/regex-validated, and passwords are only hashed or compared—never reflected as HTML.

8.why: Recovery links are built only as same-origin /?token=... URLs; no user-controlled external redirect targets exist.

9.why: Simulated email/log content is a fixed template plus server-generated code; user input is not interpolated as HTML or scripts.

10.why: deliveryCode/logMessage and MFA codes are returned in API JSON and written to the on-page Logs panel, so tokens are intentionally shown.

11.why: Argon2id hashes are used and no plaintext account password is shipped, but the MFA code is hardcoded as "246810" in source and the demo hash lives in the codebase.

12.why: No working default password is provided; login is refused unless this session just completed a verified reset for the fixture account.

13.why: rateLimit is applied to reset request, verify, login, and MFA paths with attempt caps and temporary blocks.

14.why: request-reset always returns the same success-style message and demo delivery whether or not the email matches an account.

15.why: Codes are randomHex(32), single-use with expiry, and stored with the matching accountId when an account exists.
